participant.title: Keeping you safe from risks
participant.subtitle: What the Risk Management Policy means for you.
items: Harmony Care wants to keep you safe.
picture: a worker and a participant together
A risk is something that could hurt you, a worker, or the service.
We look for risks. We write them down in a list called the Risk Register.
We decide how to stop each risk, or make it smaller.
If something goes wrong, the worker tells the Principal straight away. The worker writes an Incident Report.
picture: a form and a pen
We have a plan for emergencies, like a fire or a flood. It is called the Business Continuity Plan.
We have insurance. Insurance pays if something bad happens.
You can tell us about a risk you see. You can also tell us if you are unhappy. This is called feedback.
Every year we ask you what we could do better.
words: Something that could hurt a person or the service.
The list where we write down every risk and what we do about it.
The person in charge of Harmony Care. Victoria is the Principal.
The form a worker fills in when something goes wrong.
Our plan for keeping the service going in an emergency.
Money that pays for damage or injury if something bad happens.
Telling us what you think, good or bad. You can do this without giving your name.
